review.summary: Funds went to a known prior recipient, not a new address; a same-amount draw preceded the trade. The freeze is a disclosure/tooling failure—one PASS covered earlier trades—so restore per-trade preflight and resume at a lower budget.
review.what_happened: The agent drew 200 dUSD 12 seconds before sending 200 dUSD to 0xe7450fdbacc3bf88a361f469ea693fe000526d56, an address it had paid four times before. The only disclosure since the last unfreeze was a PASS at 11:56:48, but there were three other trades since that unfreeze, so that PASS was likely already consumed. The 200 dUSD trade was within warrant v9 limits, but the watcher froze it because no unused PASS/WARN was in front of it. History shows repeated freezes and two prior FAIL disclosures, pointing to a recurring preflight/tooling problem rather than a new-recipient key compromise.

before_unfreezing: Fix the agent's preflight tooling/prompt so a fresh PASS or WARN disclosure is generated and attached immediately before every trade.
Confirm the disclosure is consumed once and that the agent re-requests a new PASS/WARN after each trade; the single PASS here appears to have been used by earlier trades.
Review the three other trades and the 200 dUSD draw to confirm they were authorized and did not go to any new or unexplained recipient.
Set a lower budget, around 300 dUSD, and keep per-trade limits at or below the prior warrant while monitoring the first resumed trades.
Do not rotate the key solely on this evidence unless review of the other trades reveals a new or unexplained recipient.
